key_bets: Synchronized pneumatic piston array can compress a flowing liquid metal vortex at commercial scale (~4 m cavity) with <1% timing error across dozens-to-hundreds of pistons
12:1 cavity volume compression ratio is achievable in flowing liquid metal (currently only 8:1 demonstrated in water surrogate tests)
Commercial repetition rate of ~1 Hz is reachable from the current ~1 shot/day LM26 demonstration (86,400× gap)
Self-renewing liquid metal liner (Li or PbLi) provides combined breeding (TBR ~1.5), neutron absorption, and heat transfer functions without a separate blanket or solid first wall
Compact toroid (spherical torus) plasma injector can deliver consistent shot-to-shot plasma quality at 1 Hz over 10^8 pulse lifetime
Plasma physics demonstrated on the LM26 electromagnetic theta-pinch surrogate transfers to the mechanically-driven commercial system despite fundamentally different drive mechanisms
Fusion gain Q and thermal efficiency will be sufficient for net positive generation after recirculating power (piston recharge, CT injector, LM pumping)
eliminated_costs: HTS superconducting magnet system and associated cryoplant (CAS22 magnets ≈ $0 vs. $1–3B for ARC-class tokamak) — confinement provided by mechanical compression of liquid metal
Per-shot target/liner consumables (liquid metal reforms each pulse; no target factory analogous to IFE/MagLIF's ~28M targets/year)
Separate solid first-wall blanket fabrication and scheduled PFC replacement (liquid metal liner is self-renewing and serves as combined breeder + heat carrier)
REBCO tape supply chain dependency ($30–100/kA-m) that constrains tokamak/stellarator concepts
Beryllium and FLiBe supply/toxicity constraints (pure Li or PbLi design avoids beryllium entirely)
novel_costs: Pneumatic compression driver system (piston array + steam recharge infrastructure + vessel) — $180M baseline with $50M–$500M+ range; no industrial analogue at 4 m scale / 1 Hz / activated liquid metal environment
Synchronized piston timing, seal, and wear management under combined steam pressure, shock loading, and neutron-activated environment (~3×10^7 cycles/year)
Double-walled intermediate heat exchangers for Li/PbLi-to-steam interface to manage tritium permeation and Li-water reactivity (analogous to sodium-cooled fast reactor IHX)
Liquid metal vortex formation, stability, and sub-second reformation at commercial cavity scale
Compact toroid plasma injector at 1 Hz duty cycle — no equivalent injector at this rep rate; lifetime and replacement cost unknown

risks.description: FM-1: 12:1 compression ratio cannot be achieved in flowing liquid metal at commercial cavity diameter (only 8:1 demonstrated in water surrogate) — binary physics viability failure eliminating the concept

FM-2: Synchronized pneumatic piston operation proves mechanically infeasible at commercial scale due to vortex instability, timing scatter, or acoustic asymmetry — no fallback compression mechanism in current design
Rep rate gap of ~86,400× between LM26 (~1 shot/day) and commercial target (1 Hz); shortfall propagates linearly into LCOE (0.5 Hz doubles capital $/kWh)
Fusion gain Q entirely undisclosed — energy balance structurally underdetermined; minimum Q ≳ 1/η_thermal required for breakeven, Q ≳ 5–10 likely needed for commercial viability
Compression system capital cost unknown with no industrial analogue; likely dominant non-blanket capital account ranging $50M (optimistic) to $500M+ (novel engineering premium)
Capacity factor for novel piston-and-vortex mechanical architecture at 1 Hz is unpublished; unplanned downtime could push CF to 50–60%, the dominant LCOE penalty relative to MFE concepts
Li-6 enrichment supply chain risk — no large-scale Western capacity exists for fusion-fleet quantities (historically Russia/China)
Liquid metal composition (Li vs. PbLi) unresolved; first-order LCOE branching decision affecting ISS capital, safety infrastructure, tritium permeation, and neutron multiplication
Tritium permeation through Li/PbLi-to-steam generator interface; pure Li reacts violently with water requiring costly intermediate heat exchangers
LM26 electromagnetic theta-pinch demonstration is a scientific surrogate that does not validate the commercial pneumatic engineering — TRL of demo is not transferable
Piston seal and wear performance under combined steam pressure, shock loading, and activated liquid metal environment is unqualified; no materials data exists for this combined loading
Tritium startup inventory (1–5 kg) dependent on declining CANDU supply (~22 kg global, shared with all D-T fusion concepts)
